CVX.rationale: CVX is extremely unattractive at current levels. Earnings have collapsed: Q1 2026 EPS of $1.11 is down -44.5% YoY, operating income fell -29.2%, and operating cash flow dropped -51.6% to $2.51B. This is a profitability problem, not a revenue problem — revenue was actually +2.1% YoY, but costs below the gross-profit line consumed the improvement. ROE has nearly halved from 10.5% to 5.9%, and net margin sits at 5.9%, the floor of its 365-day window. Meanwhile, the stock trades at a trailing P/E of 32.4x — the 93rd percentile of its 365-day range — meaning the market is paying a historically full multiple for deteriorating earnings power. The earnings yield of 3.1% is well below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.57%, offering no compensation for cyclicality. WTI crude has declined ~29% from its May peak to $80.03, directly pressuring future upstream realizations and suggesting further earnings risk. The balance sheet (D/E 0.74x) is not stressed, but with OCF of only $2.51B against $140B+ in liabilities, coverage depends on a cash-flow recovery that the numbers have not yet validated. The qualitative franchise is solid — integrated model, Permian + Guyana assets, fortress balance sheet, AI data center power deal — but these structural strengths are already embedded in the elevated multiple. Q2 earnings (due late July) could be a de-risking event, but UBS's $5.70 EPS estimate would still represent a significant decline from prior-year levels, and the near-term catalyst does not offset the combination of deteriorating fundamentals, stretched valuation, and a falling oil price backdrop. All three pillars — deteriorating fundamentals, expensive valuation vs. own history, and macro headwinds from falling WTI — are aligned bearishly.
